postings.text: P-1346 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. Databricks Mosaic AI offers a unique data-centric approach to building enterprise-quality, Machine Learning and Generative AI solutions, enabling organizations to securely and cost-effectively own and host ML and Generative AI models, augmented or trained with their enterprise data. The Money team's mission at Databricks is to maximize the value that our customers derive from their investments in data projects. We accomplish this through innovative commercialisation strategies, timely & accurate billing, cost optimisation tools, intelligent resource usage controls, and cutting-edge engineering. We provide a seamless and consistent experience set of platforms for all Databricks products to reach customers. As one of the first engineers for Money at Databricks India , you will be key to building a base for one of Databricks’ most central engineering teams . You will own critical components that form the backbone of our products, starting with Databricks’ resource admission control and usage governance infrastructure . Your role is crucial in helping bring diverse business needs together, including abuse prevention, product commercialisation motions, and reliable product availability at scale. You will work closely with infrastructure as well as product teams in bringing critical governance functionality to Databricks customers. The impact you will have: Own Money systems and services that govern usage of all Databricks products and offerings. Enhance engineering and infrastructure efficiency, reliability, accuracy, and response times, including CI/CD processes, test frameworks, data quality assurance, end-to-end reconciliation, and anomaly detection. Collaborate with platform and product teams to develop and implement innovative infrastructure that scales to meet evolving needs. Provide leadership in long-term vision and requirements development for Databricks products, in partnership with our engineering teams. Represent Databricks at academic and industrial conferences & events. What we look for: BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, or a related field 12+ years of production level experience in one of: Java, Scala, C++, or similar language. Comfortable working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables. Proven track record in architecting, developing, deploying, and operating large scale distributed systems. Experience with software security and systems that handle sensitive data. Demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to lead across functional and organizational boundaries. A proactive approach and a passion for delivering high-quality solutions Experience with cloud technologies, e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP, Docker, Kubernetes. Our mission is to simplify how data is connected, understood, and activated so that organizations can turn information into business outcomes. postings.text: (GAQ427R229) About the role AI is the defining platform shift of our generation, and Databricks is right at the center of it. We are looking for a Product Finance leader to scale the fastest growing part of our business with both speed and financial rigor. You will be the primary finance partner to our AI Engineering and Product leaders, with a mandate that spans the full arc of the AI business: planning GPU supply and demand across clouds, shaping how we price AI products, and building the unit economics that will define the margins of this category for years to come. The impact you will have Plan the GPU supply and demand that powers the business Establish a trusted, unified GPU demand plan across production inference, internal research, and new product bets so we invest ahead of growth without over-provisioning. Drive capacity commitment and procurement strategies across major hyperscalers and emerging neoclouds, optimizing the mix of reserved, spot, and on-demand compute. Own AI product economics and partner on pricing Lead revenue and margin analytics across the AI product portfolio, turning raw consumption telemetry into a clear read on customer adoption, retention, and product profitability. Model the end-to-end unit economics of AI products before they ship, partnering with Product and Pricing to design consumption structures that drive adoption while protecting gross margin targets. Establish robust KPIs and operations to drive best-in-class execution Partner with Engineering to define north star efficiency KPIs (e.g., GPU utilization, cost per token/query, serverless efficiency) and translate them into committed engineering roadmaps. Run tight financial operations, from auditable multi-cloud cost allocation to automated reporting, giving product and engineering leaders real-time visibility into their economic goals. Bring finance rigor to the biggest investment decisions Design ROI and capital allocation frameworks to evaluate asymmetric bets—including frontier model research, internal compute clusters, and strategic partnerships. Deep fluency in consumption-based business models, public cloud infrastructure costs, unit cost analysis, and gross margin optimization. A proven track record of partnering directly with senior Engineering and Product executives to influence technical roadmaps and commercial pricing. Demonstrated ability to build scalable financial systems from scratch and distill massive, complex telemetry data into models and recommendations leaders act on. Experience building, leading, and developing high-output finance teams in fast-moving environments. Preferred Direct experience operating in the AI and GPU economy, including familiarity with training/inference workloads, hyperscaler commitment structures, and neocloud economics. postings.title: Director, Field Engineering (CPG & Retail)
postings.text: REQ ID: FEQ427R375 Mission: As the Director of Field Engineering, you will be responsible for partnering with our enterprise Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and Retail customers to democratize Data and AI within their organizations, leveraging Databricks solutions and expertise to address their most critical business challenges. Reporting to the Tech GM of Field Engineering for Retail & Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), the Director, Field Engineering will lead a team of pre-sales Managers and Solutions Architects focused on acquiring new customers and expanding strategic relationships across the Retail and CPG industry. You will work closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and executive stakeholders to drive strategy and execution against our ambitious growth goals. You will foster a culture of psychological safety while developing and scaling a high-performing team with expertise in enterprise software, data engineering, analytics, AI/ML, and cloud technologies. Your experience partnering with Sales will help drive complex enterprise opportunities while coaching managers and field engineering teams to deliver exceptional customer outcomes. You will guide your team through strategic engagements, communicate complex technical solutions in terms of business value, support enterprise sales cycles, and build trusted relationships with senior business and technology leaders across the Retail and CPG industry. The impact you will have: Hire and manage first-line Managers and a growing team of technical pre-sales Solutions Architects. Build a collaborative culture within a rapid-growth team. Embody and promote Databricks' customer-obsessed, truth-seeking, diverse culture, and first principles mindset. Develop trusted, long-term executive relationships with customers while maintaining a deep understanding of the Retail and CPG industry, including key business trends, competitive dynamics, and digital transformation priorities. Help customers accelerate their Data and AI strategies across areas such as customer experience, merchandising, supply chain, demand forecasting, marketing, and operations. Promote a solution- and value-based Field Engineering organization. Display an understanding of customer business priorities and revenue opportunities across the assigned region and industry. Serve as a thought leader for Databricks and within the Retail, CPG, Data, and AI ecosystem. What we look for: At least 3 years of second-line leadership experience managing teams of 30+ individuals, with 10+ years of overall leadership experience. Proven success leading high-growth enterprise software pre-sales organizations within Retail, CPG, cloud, data, analytics, or AI. Experience partnering with Retail and/or CPG customers on large-scale data, analytics, AI, or digital transformation initiatives. Ability to elevate executive engagement, with a track record of driving large strategic transactions and expanding high-growth enterprise accounts. Proven leadership ability to influence, develop, and empower teams to achieve ambitious business objectives through collaboration. Drive operational rigor to manage a high-growth business, establishing the right operating cadence while ensuring visibility into customer priorities, escalations, and product feedback. Proven track record of delivering transformational customer outcomes and measurable business value. Track record of building strong customer relationships and cross-functional partnerships across Sales, Engineering, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success. Experience positioning technical solutions within complex enterprise environments and helping customers realize long-term value and platform adoption with Databricks. Strong operational leadership with experience implementing scalable processes that improve the effectiveness and productivity of technical field organizations. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

postings.text: CSQ127R319 As a Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you will work with customers to build and productionize solutions to their data & AI challenges using the Databricks platform. You will own the architecture, lead design decisions, and implement end-to-end systems spanning data engineering, AI, and application development. We work cross-functionally to shape long-term strategic priorities and initiatives alongside engineering, product, and developer relations. FDEs deliver with customer empathy, integrating with client systems, training, and other technical needs to help customers get most value out of their data. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. The ideal candidate combines engineering expertise with adaptability, curiosity, and a passion for working with customers and teammates to solve complex problems that drive measurable outcomes. FDEs are billable and know how to complete projects according to specification with exceptional customer empathy. The impact you will have: Production Solution Delivery: Lead impactful customer technical projects by delivering production-grade systems, designing and building reference architectures, custom applications and data ingestion and ML/AI model integration Transformational Impact: Guide strategic customers as they implement transformational big data projects including end-to-end design, build and deployment of industry-leading big data and AI applications. Work with engagement managers to scope technical delivery work with input from the customer Empower Customers: Guide customers on architecture and design; bootstrap or implement customer projects which leads to a customers' successful understanding, evaluation and adoption of Databricks. Own the Architecture: Lead architecture and design decisions, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Databricks best practices. Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs. Work with Engineering and Databricks Customer Support to provide product and implementation feedback and to guide rapid resolution for engagement specific product and support issues. Customer Immersion: Embed with customer teams, engaging with stakeholders from technical ICs to executives to deeply understand challenges and deliver impact. Reusable Assets & Scale: Contribute accelerators, frameworks, and best practices that scale impact across accounts and influence the Databricks product roadmap. What we look for: 6+ years experience in data engineering, data platforms & analytics, or software engineering Comfortable writing code in either Python, Scala, JavaScript/TypeScript, and modern frameworks Working knowledge of two or more common Cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP) with expertise in at least one Deep experience with distributed computing with Apache Spark™ and knowledge of Spark runtime internals Familiarity with CI/CD for production deployments Working knowledge of MLOps, ML/AI models and AI APIs Design and deployment of performant production end-to-end data architectures and applications that combine data pipelines, ML/AI models, and user-facing interfaces. Experience with technical project delivery - managing scope, timelines and measurable outcomes, translating complex concepts into actionable solutions. Documentation and white-boarding skills. Experience working with enterprise clients and managing conflicts across a broad stakeholder range Build skills in technical areas, and demonstrate curiosity, adaptability, and eagerness to explore new technologies which support the deployment and integration of Databricks-based solutions to complete customer projects. Travel to customers 20% of the time Databricks Certification Pay Range Transparency Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices

postings.title: Staff Software Engineer, Technical Lead, Lakebase Manager (LBM)
postings.text: P-988 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers and customer obsessed, we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started. Lakebase enables teams to deliver applications faster with an optimized database developer experience, integration with the lakehouse, and simplified operations. It provides a managed Postgres transactional layer for application state and workloads that combine operational data, analytics, and AI. You'll join as one of the key engineers building out the Lakebase product. As the Technical Lead on the Lakebase Manager (LBM) team, you will drive, build, and operate the central control plane that owns the core logic for Lakebase: database creation and deletion, wake-up and suspend, maintaining computes on hot standby, HA failover, and more. LBM interacts with every Lakebase component (storage, compute, proxy, and console) and manages the full database lifecycle at scale, with a focus on reliability. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role: you lead the team technically and partner with the team's engineering manager, who owns people management and delivery planning. The stack is Go, Rust, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes. The impact you will have: Set the technical direction for LBM and own the quality and reliability of what the team ships, driving execution on the hardest, highest-risk parts. Drive architecture and design, and write code on the hardest parts of your team's projects. Set and uphold high technical standards through architecture reviews, testing, and a culture of engineering excellence. Raise the technical bar of the team: mentor engineers, drive rigorous design and code review, and grow their distributed-systems and design skills. Define SLIs, meet SLOs, and drive long-term reliability improvements across the database lifecycle. Lead cross-team initiatives across the Lakebase stack: align with partner teams on dependencies and unblock cross-cutting projects. Partner with engineering and product leadership to shape and deliver a long-term technical roadmap. What we look for: 8+ years designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems, including the processes around testing, monitoring, and SLIs/SLOs. A track record of technical leadership as an individual contributor: setting architecture and direction for a team's projects through influence, without formal management authority. Strong hands-on depth: you still design systems and write production code, and can go deep on architecture for large-scale distributed services. Experience operating reliability-critical, highly available services (on-call, incident response, HA/failover). Comfortable working toward a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables, and balancing short-term delivery against long-term stability. Ability to align multiple stakeholders on competing priorities. Motivated by delivering customer value and impact. Proficiency in Go, Rust, or a similar systems language; experience with PostgreSQL and Kubernetes is a plus. BS (or higher) in Computer Science, or a related field. postings.text: Datadog AI Research — Scholars Program with Carnegie Mellon University Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR. You will frame a problem, run your own experiments, and write up what you find, with compute and data at a scale most academic labs cannot provide. You will collaborate with colleagues working on the same questions. The Lab And The Research: DAIR is an industrial research lab motivated by practical challenges in observability and software operation: detecting and diagnosing failures, understanding complex production environments, and helping engineers operate software more effectively. The lab focuses on creating specialized foundation models, post-training and evaluating AI agents, and building frontier-scale machine learning systems. By combining fundamental research with Datadog's large-scale, real-world data and infrastructure, the lab develops new AI capabilities and translates them into practical systems with meaningful impact. Internship projects are shaped with your DAIR mentor and your CMU faculty advisor. You do not need prior experience with observability, monitoring, or infrastructure. What You'll Do: Own a research project end to end: framing the question, running the experiments, writing it up Work directly with a DAIR mentor engaged in the same problem, and stay connected to your advisor and lab Publish, and use the work toward your dissertation See research reach production, when it works Who You Are: Currently enrolled in a PhD program at Carnegie Mellon in machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a related field Depth in at least one area relevant to the research above Comfort running real experiments — training models, working with GPUs, reading and reimplementing recent papers Evidence you can do research: conference or workshop papers, preprints, open-source contributions, or a lab project you can discuss in depth Research taste. You can explain why a problem matters and what would change if it were solved. Honest empiricism. You report the ablation that didn't work. Support from your faculty advisor. Not Required: A long publication record. How you think matters more than how much you've published. Observability, monitoring, or SRE background. A perfect match to the areas above. postings.text: The Staff Product Manager is an Individual Contributor (IC) product leader responsible for a broad platform surface for Atlas Infinite at MongoDB. Atlas Infinite is the largest architectural innovation in MongoDB Atlas ever, purpose-built to handle today's speed and scale of development and demand. In this position, you will own and solve end-to-end problems around the user experience and database experience of Atlas Infinite, including but limited to feature discovery, activation, monetization, and retention. You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering leaders, product peers, and executive stakeholders to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries, guiding a portfolio spanning Atlas Infinite's disaggregated compute and storage architecture, production workload readiness, migration and Atlas interoperability, and the new customer experiences this architecture may make possible. You will not inherit a closed list of future features: part of your mandate is to discover opportunities we have not yet articulated and challenge assumptions about which problems matter most. postings.text: MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real. We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users. This role can be based remotely in Ontario, Canada. About the Storage Execution team The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads. The team’s responsibilities include: Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations What you’ll do Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; postings.text: MongoDB is at an important moment. AI is changing how applications are built, how technology gets selected, and what enterprises expect from their data infrastructure. We have a strong point of view on where this is going. We need a communications leader who can help us make that point of view matter in the market. This is not a traditional corporate communications role. You will work closely with the CMO, CEO, and our technical leaders to sharpen the ideas we want to be known for and make sure they reach the people — and increasingly the AI systems — shaping technology decisions. This role will lead the evolution of communications for an AI-mediated world—using traditional media, creators, technical media, podcasts, and other trusted voices to shape what people think and influence the sources AI systems use to generate answers and recommendations. This role may be based in a hybrid capacity at any of our U.S. offices or fully remote within the United States. From launches, keynotes and earnings to partnerships, competitive moments and reputation issues. Bring together market insight, product positioning and proof, and developer perspective into one coherent narrative, then lead the media, analyst and influencer strategy, timing and execution that makes it land Leading the global communications team: Build and lead a strong team across corporate, executive, product, analyst, social, internal, and regional communications, with a clear global strategy that works across markets What we are looking for You have excellent judgment and create the agenda. You can take in a lot of information and quickly figure out what matters, what doesn’t, and where the real story is. You proactively raise ideas and opportunities and turn them into action. You understand the technology and the industry. You are fluent enough in AI, application architecture, and data infrastructure to engage credibly with technical executives, developers, product leaders, technical media, and analysts You know how influence works to drive outcomes. You will design and implement the fundamental transformations infrastructure—Stateful Stream Processing Engines, Incremental View Maintenance Engine, Materialization Internals, and the Distributed Orchestration Fabric. Our solid foundation supporting the seamless transition for enterprises between batch and streaming through Dynamic Tables, Streams & Tasks, and DBT Projects is the starting point. Your architectural work will extend the reach of the core engine to accelerate and support the massive scale of the Snowpark and Spark ecosystems. You are building the systems that allow both data engineers and autonomous agents to process exabytes of data with sub-second state propagation and absolute transactional integrity across the Snowflake Data Cloud. postings.text: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Compute Foundation group builds and operates the core systems that enable every Stripe engineer to ship code, configuration, and infrastructure changes safely and at high velocity. Embedded on the Imaging team, you will design, build, and distribute Linux machine images; manage host bootstrapping and OS-configuration systems; oversee OS packages and security-patching infrastructure; and provide platforms that empower service teams to safely run workloads across cloud providers and regions. What you’ll do Own the foundation of Stripe’s compute fleet: Stripe’s services rely on host infrastructure that boots reliably, receives accurate configurations, and operates safely. Your decisions will directly shape the base operating system, package ecosystems, security posture, and bootstrap behavior of Stripe’s fleet. Lead active architectural transformations: The team is driving key platform evolutions, including modernizing the OS configuration layer, containerizing workloads, scaling machine image distribution across multi-cloud regions, and streamlining OS upgrades and critical security patching. Drive broad, end-to-end host lifecycle ownership: Work across the entire host lifecycle - from image construction, package distribution, kernel and OS configuration, early boot/systemd, storage, networking initialization, and workload readiness. You will tackle complex engineering challenges that balance reliability, security, compliance, developer experience, and performance. The Duolingo English Test (DET) is a high-stakes assessment used by institutions around the world. Its integrity depends on proctors making accurate, consistent, and defensible decisions — even when sessions present ambiguous evidence or new forms of cheating. As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program. 🧠 You will... Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases. Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable. Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes. Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance. Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly. Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable. Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering. Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality. Labs focuses on a broad variety of AI/ML initiatives, such as core computer vision, multimodal representation learning, heterogeneous graph neural networks, generative modeling, recommender systems, etc. This is the group that develops foundation ML models that fully leverage the tens of billions of Pins and the associated knowledge graph to improve the core product. Canvas is a foundation text-to-image model developed internally for helping various visualization, inpainting, and outpainting products. In this role, you’ll get to work with Pinterest’s rich visual-text dataset to build large-scale generative models which are continuously being shipped to production to power visualization features. What you’ll do: Prototype new model architectures for Pinterest Canvas, our internal text-to-image generative model. We’re looking for hands-on experience working with diffusion text-to-image models and independent model implementation skills. Read research papers, participate in group discussions, and help brainstorm our overall visual generative strategy at the company. Help with collection of relevant visual training data for Pinterest Canvas, particularly to conduct RLHF, targeted fine-tuning, etc. Publish and publicize your work via conferences, paper submissions, blog posts, etc. Mentor more junior researchers or research interns within the Pinterest Labs organization. What we’re looking for: Research engineers and scientists who have experience working with generative computer vision models, preferably various forms of diffusion models. 5+ years of industry computer vision experience. Experience using Cursor, Copilot, Codex, or similar AI coding assistants for development, debugging, testing, and refactoring. postings.title: Systems Engineer, New Restaurant Openings
postings.text: sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthy communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone, and we are building a company that reflects that belief. Our team is made up of people who care deeply about the guest experience, our partners, and each other. The Systems Engineer II, New Restaurant Openings is responsible for the technical build out of new and relocated sweetgreen restaurants. The role sits on the NRO team within Technology and works at the intersection of business systems analysis and hands on technical execution: partnering with Store Design, Operations, and third party vendors, translating restaurant requirements into system configuration, then staging, configuring, and validating the restaurant technology stack so that each location opens with technology that works the first time. That stack includes POS and QSR platforms such as PAR Brink, along with payments, loyalty, inventory, Salesforce, and the integrations between them. You will be a technical point of contact at each NRO milestone, and you will help reduce the manual effort in the process over time through scripting, API driven tooling, and templated configuration. You will: Execute the technical build out for assigned new restaurant openings, from requirements through go live and post launch stabilization, working alongside the third party vendors who perform on site installation. Configure POS and QSR platforms for each opening, including menus, pricing, tenders, modifiers, and store level settings, and stage back end systems and environments so all platforms are integration-ready before go-live. Validate technical readiness at each NRO milestone, including install, punch, turnover, and pre-grand opening, against defined entry and exit criteria, and escalate risk early rather than at the gate. Provide on-site and remote support during opening week, troubleshoot configuration, integration, and data flow issues across POS, payments, loyalty, inventory, and reporting, and transition each location cleanly into steady-state IT support. Build automation that removes manual steps from the build, including scripting, REST API integrations, and bulk configuration tooling, and execute functional, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing with results captured as repeatable artifacts. Gather and document requirements from Restaurant Operations, Finance, Construction, and Development partners, translate them into system configuration, and report readiness and status clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Desired traits: Detail-driven: you treat configuration accuracy as the product, and you verify rather than assume. Range from planning to execution: you flex from documentation and requirements work to hands-on troubleshooting depending on what the opening requires. Calm under a fixed deadline: openings do not move, and you stay steady and clear-headed in the final week. Systems thinker: you look for the pattern behind a recurring issue instead of fixing the same thing store by store. Automation-minded: you would rather script a task than repeat it, and you look for the manual work worth eliminating. Trusted partner: you communicate technical risk credibly to operators and business leaders without jargon. Ownership: you follow an opening through to a stable handoff rather than to the point of technical completion. Desired experience: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience. 3 to 5+ years in systems engineering, business systems analysis, or technical implementation, ideally within restaurant, retail, or QSR technology. Hands-on configuration experience with POS and QSR platforms, with PAR Brink, QSR Automation preferred and Toast, Aloha, or Oracle Micros comparable, including menu, pricing, tender, and store-level configuration. postings.title: Marketing Manager
postings.text: BRAND MANAGER, MARKETING sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthier communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day in each sweetgreen, our 5,000 team members make food from scratch, using fresh ingredients and produce delivered that morning. And in our local communities, we’re committed to leaving people better than we found them. We’re in the business of feeding people, and we’re out to change what that means. Our teams are our most valuable ingredient - the heart of our company, the face of our brand, and what truly makes the sweetgreen experience special and unique. The Brand Marketing Manager will play an integral role in shaping the future of sweetgreen by serving as a key stakeholder in brand strategy and execution. This position will leverage their proven track record to lead and support breakthrough brand communications campaigns, including go-to-market product launch strategies, guest engagement promotions, and brand experiences and innovations. The role will also play a key part in menu innovation and channel strategy to build the sweetgreen brand. The Brand Marketing Manager will report to the Brand Marketing team. You’ll be joining a team that manages multiple high-stakes campaigns with a guest-obsessed, culturally driven mindset. Join us for the opportunity to make your mark on the future of food. As the Brand Marketing Manager, you will: Lead new product launches and go-to-market campaigns by contributing consumer-insight driven, breakthrough strategies and briefs, ensuring flawless consumer experience across all media touchpoints and in-restaurant. Manage internal and external partners, including experiential, PR, social, digital, media, and tech teams to execute the successful launch of brand campaigns. Oversee brand strategy and off-premise packaging and product innovation, driving impact and measuring success against established KPIs. Foster a high-functioning working relationship with Consumer Insights and our internal Creative team to bring breakthrough and insight-based creative communications strategies and campaigns to life. Drive decision-making through a spirit of business ownership -- contributing a clear financial understanding of the business. Assess the continuous evolution of the competitive landscape, consumer insights, new societal trends, and culture. Desired traits: Experience in Brand or Product Marketing, Integrated Communications, Cultural Marketing, and managing complex initiatives Strong communication, attention to detail and organizational skills Successful track record of program and promotion execution Exceptional interpersonal, communication, cross-collaboration, and team skills Ability to solve problems both independently and as part of a team Curious and positively resilient Experience in using consumer insights and data to drive decision-making Experience working with (and maintains active connections with) internal and external creative teams and agency partners Desired experience: Minimum 4-Year degree, MBA Preferred Minimum 3-5 years of Brand-Building and Culturally-Driven Integrated Marketing Communications Experience What you'll get: Highly competitive pay + bonus plan Three different medical plans to suit your and your family's needs Dental and Vision insurance Flexible PTO plan 401k program Employee HSA and FSA Complimentary greens An opportunity to make a real impact on the people around you, both by growing them and by connecting them to real food To live the sweetlife and celebrate your passion + purpose A collaborative team of people who live our core values and have your back A clear career path with opportunities for development, both personally and professionally Free sweetgreen swag Come join the sweetlife! postings.title: Senior Loss Prevention Manager
postings.text: sweetgreen is on a mission to build healthy communities by connecting people to real food. We passionately believe that real food should be convenient and accessible to everyone. Every day in each sweetgreen, our 5,000+ team members make food from scratch, using fresh ingredients and produce delivered that morning. And in our local communities, we're committed to leaving people better than we found them. We're looking for a Senior Loss Prevention Manager to own loss prevention, physical security, and crisis and resiliency planning across sweetgreen's restaurants and support centers. Sitting on the Operations Services team and reporting to the Senior Director of Risk + Safety, you will lead our camera and investigations program, drive shrink and fraud reduction, manage physical security across our locations, and build the playbooks and response capability that keep our people, guests, and operations safe when things go wrong. This role is based onsite at our Los Angeles Support Center. You will: Own the loss prevention program end to end, driving strategy to reduce shrink, theft, and fraud, and managing the camera and video investigations platform, case work, and evidence retention. Lead investigations into suspected internal and external theft, fraud, and policy violations, partnering with the People and Legal Teams on outcomes. Set and maintain physical security standards across restaurants and support centers (access control, camera coverage, alarms), manage security vendors and guard services, and oversee incident response for events such as break-ins, theft, and workplace violence. Build and maintain crisis response, business continuity, and resiliency plans, and serve as a lead responder during active crises, coordinating across Operations, Communications, People, and Legal. Manage loss prevention, security, and investigations against service expectations and budget, and support the annual insurance renewal with loss and incident data. Maintain incident data and reporting, produce trend dashboards for leadership, and ensure practices comply with federal, state, and local requirements across all jurisdictions. Desired traits: A calm, decisive presence during active incidents, with the judgment to lead a response while keeping the right people informed. A prevention mindset, building the systems and training that stop incidents before they happen rather than only responding after the fact. Strong analytical fluency, able to read loss, incident, and security data and turn it into recommendations leadership can act on. Highly organized with strong follow-through, able to manage a broad, fast-moving portfolio and competing priorities. A clear, credible communicator who works well with field operators, executives, vendors, and law enforcement. Sound judgment about when to act within authority and when to escalate to Risk + Safety leadership. Desired experience: 7+ years in loss prevention, physical security, or corporate security, ideally in multi-unit retail, restaurant, or hospitality. Working knowledge of loss prevention investigations, camera and exception-based reporting systems, and physical security standards. Experience managing security, investigations, or loss prevention vendors and guard services. Experience with crisis management or business continuity planning is a plus. Knowledge of multi-jurisdictional security and safety requirements. Relevant certifications (CPP, PCI, CFI, or similar) are a plus. What you'll get: Highly competitive pay + bonus plan Three different medical plans to suit your and your family's needs Dental and Vision insurance Flexible PTO plan 401k program Employee HSA and FSA Complimentary greens An opportunity to make a real impact on the people around you, both by growing them and by connecting them to real food To live the sweetlife and celebrate your passion + purpose A collaborative team of people who live our core values and have your back A clear career path with opportunities for develo

postings.title: Quality Engineer
postings.text: Build quality into every product and help shape the future of AI-powered software. As a quality engineer at Gallup, you'll help deliver software our clients can trust by partnering with product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of the software development life cycle. Rather than simply executing test cases, you'll apply systems thinking to identify risks, develop thoughtful validation strategies and help ensure every release delivers an exceptional customer experience. As Gallup continues to expand its AI-powered products, you'll also have opportunities to contribute to testing intelligent workflows and emerging AI capabilities. What You’ll Do Develop a deep understanding of product features, customer workflows, system interactions, APIs, data flows, integrations and technical dependencies to identify quality risks and determine the most effective validation strategy Collaborate within Gallup's Product Operating Model alongside product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of product development Design, execute and maintain manual and automated tests across user interfaces, APIs, integrations and end-to-end workflows Develop and maintain automated test suites using Playwright or comparable modern automation frameworks Perform exploratory, regression, smoke and end-to-end testing to uncover system risks and validate critical customer experiences Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines to provide fast, reliable feedback throughout development Troubleshoot automation failures and partner with engineering teams to improve test stability, reliability and automation coverage Create and maintain test plans and traceability that reflect product intent, customer impact and overall validation strategy Support production validation and investigate customer-reported issues when needed Continuously improve quality engineering practices, automation capabilities and release confidence What Makes You Stand Out Systems thinking: You naturally connect product features, APIs, integrations and customer workflows to identify risks before they become production issues. Quality-first mindset: You view quality engineering as an integral part of software development and proactively build quality into products rather than testing only at the end. Automation expertise: You develop maintainable, scalable automated testing solutions that improve release confidence and accelerate delivery. Collaborative partnerships: You build strong relationships across Product, Engineering and Design teams, communicating effectively to solve complex problems and improve outcomes. Continuous learning: You embrace emerging technologies, modern testing approaches and AI-enabled engineering practices while continually expanding your technical expertise. What You Need Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, information systems or a related field, or equivalent professional experience required At least three years of experience in quality engineering, including both functional and automated testing, required Experience testing web applications and REST APIs required Experience developing automated tests using Playwright, Cypress, Selenium or comparable automation frameworks required Experience working within Agile software development teams required Familiarity with Git and CI/CD pipelines required Experience using test management platforms such as QMetry, Azure DevOps Test Plans or TestRail required Experience with TypeScript/JavaScript and/or Python preferred Experience with SQL and database validation preferred Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure preferred Experience with performance, security or data quality testing preferred Experience contributing to automation frameworks and reusable testing utilities preferred Experience testing AI-powered applications, chatbots, copilots or intelligent workflow

Our teams build real-time money movement and decisioning infrastructure at scale, including underwriting and eligibility, ledgering and reconciliation, capital markets workflows, repayment systems, and financial transactions that must be correct, resilient, and auditable. As a Software Engineer in Lending, you’ll work at the seam between member-facing products and the platforms that make them possible. This is a role for engineers who want to own more than a single service or feature area. You’ll lead technical initiatives that cut across products, platforms, and partner teams, helping shape how Lending evolves as a system, not just how one team ships. You’ll design and build backend systems where correctness, reliability, speed, and operational rigor matter deeply. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Risk, Data Science, Analytics, Finance, and Operations to turn ambiguous opportunities into durable solutions, influence technical direction across team boundaries, and help raise the bar for how Lending engineers build together. Why join Lending? Work on systems that matter The products and platforms we build directly impact millions of members and sit at the center of Chime’s mission to help everyday people unlock financial progress. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the work matters. Own a bigger surface area This role is designed for engineers who want broader scope. You won’t be limited to a narrow feature lane. You’ll work across product experiences and shared infrastructure, helping connect strategy, systems, and execution across Lending. Build where product and platform meet Some of the most interesting engineering work happens in the seams: where member experience depends on credit strategy, where product velocity depends on platform leverage, and where financial correctness meets business speed. This role sits in the middle of those seams and gives you meaningful influence over how they scale. Operate in a fast-moving, high-accountability environment Lending is a fast-paced fintech environment where we care about moving quickly and building well. We value thoughtful design, strong engineering judgment, high-quality code, and operational excellence. We also actively use AI where it can improve quality, speed, and leverage. postings.text: About the Role We are hiring a Business Control Manager to join Chime's Compliance Business Control Management team. You will own the control strategy, business relationships, and results for the Membership, App and AI Experience, and Trust and Safety portfolios. Working with the Enterprise BCM Lead and business partners, you will translate new initiatives, existing business activities, regulatory requirements, incidents, and other changes into clear control outcomes and practical plans. This is an individual contributor role for someone who can move comfortably between strategy and delivery. You will assess current control coverage, lead material control decisions and implementation work within your portfolios, and ensure controls are validated, documented, and maintained. Business and control owners remain responsible for implementing and operating their controls; you will provide the structure, challenge, and partnership needed to produce durable results. You will also contribute across the Enterprise BCM team by supporting Enterprise work when priorities and capacity require it, and by helping identify shared exposure themes and common control approaches across portfolios. In This Role You Can Expect To Own the control strategy and coverage view for assigned portfolios, using business activities, regulatory requirements, existing controls, gaps, and dependencies to set priorities. Evaluate new initiatives and the existing environment through reviews of process or product changes, incidents, complaints, findings, and current control practices. Determine whether controls should be reused, enhanced, created, consolidated, or retired. Lead control design and implementation with business and control owners, establishing clear objectives, scope, ownership, evidence, exception handling, delivery plans, and closure criteria while keeping control ownership and operation with the business. Assess control readiness, coordinate owner attestations, and determine whether controls meet the agreed validation criteria. Arrange an independent reviewer when your involvement in implementation requires additional separation. Lead control responses to incidents, issues, complaints, and findings by connecting root causes to control gaps, establishing remediation expectations, and confirming affected controls are revalidated before closure. Maintain reliable control records and use coverage, implementation, validation, and exception data to identify recurring themes, recommend shared approaches, and communicate results and remaining exposure to leadership. Build strong relationships across business, product, engineering, operations, legal, compliance, risk, and data teams, and support bank partner reviews, audits, examinations, and other assurance activities. To Thrive in This Role You Have 7 or more years of experience in business controls, regulatory compliance, operational risk, audit, or a related discipline within financial services, fintech, or another highly regulated environment. Experience independently owning a complex portfolio or control environment, setting priorities, leading cross-functional decisions, and moving work from assessment through validated and documented closure. Demonstrated ability to evaluate business activities and control coverage, distinguish control gaps from documentation or mapping gaps, and develop practical responses. Hands-on experience designing or enhancing controls with business, product, engineering, operations, or data teams and defining the evidence needed to demonstrate that controls operate as designed. Sound knowledge of consumer financial protection and regulatory risk, including EFTA and Regulation E, TILA and Regulation Z, UDAAP, or comparable frameworks. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE The Credit Engineering team builds the systems that enable Ramp to manage credit lifecycles for businesses end-to-end, from initial underwriting through ongoing portfolio strategy optimization. As an engineer on Credit, you’ll own systems that influence $100+ billion in annual payment volume through millions of decisions across our product stack in support of the most ambitious FinTech portfolio in the United States. We are looking for a backend engineer to own the technical roadmap for underwriting, limit management, portfolio optimization, and agentic workflows. You will build robust systems, automate complex operational tasks, and maintain the high-frequency controls that power all of Ramp’s products. If you are obsessed with correctness, excited by ambiguity, and passionate about problems at the intersection of distributed systems and financial strategy, this role is for you. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Architect scalable, stateful systems for automated limit management to optimize Ramp’s charge card portfolio. - Envision and build the next generation of agents and tools that automate manual credit decisions and increase operational efficiency. - Develop high-volume, low-latency risk controls to support Ramp’s expansion into new products, customer segments, and geographies. - Design and build real-time decisioning systems spanning the entirety of a business's credit lifecycle on Ramp. - Partner closely with analysts, data scientists, and product to translate risk strategies into reliable software. postings.title: Paralegal Senior
postings.text: We are a hybrid, remote-office company dedicated to growing our talent anywhere! We have onsite locations in: Sioux Falls, SD, Phoenix, AZ, Louisville, KY, Troy, MI, Franklin, TN, Easton, PA. At Pathward, we take tremendous pride in our purpose to create financial inclusion for all™. We are a financial empowerment company that works with innovators to increase financial availability, choice, and opportunity for all. We strive to remove barriers that traditional institutions put in the way of financial access, and promote economic mobility by providing responsible, secure, high quality financial products. We are a team of problem solvers and innovators who celebrate our differences and know that our unique perspectives make us stronger and well-positioned for success. We celebrate, and embrace, our team members through our *HUMBLE*HUNGRY*SMART approach, and we believe that we are strongest when we embrace the voices of our employees, customers, partners, and the communities we serve. About the Role: The Senior Paralegal serves as a key member of the Legal team, partnering closely with attorneys and business stakeholders to support commercial and consumer lending, payments, and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) initiatives. This role combines legal operations, contract management, project coordination, and regulatory support. The successful candidate is a proactive self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment, exercises sound judgment, manages multiple priorities simultaneously, and helps drive scalable legal processes across the organization. What You Will Do: Draft, review, and negotiate financing documents and third-party contracts, consulting attorneys as needed. Review, redline, and manage template agreements, including, but not limited to NDAs, online banking agreements, ACH service agreements, wind-down letters. Review and approve loan closing packages for funding. Review marketing materials, disclosures, customer communications, and new product initiatives for legal and regulatory considerations Supporting attorneys with legal documentation and contract administration. Partner with business teams to gather information, identify issues, and facilitate efficient legal review. Manage and coordinate responses to subpoenas and other legal process requests. Provide litigation and bankruptcy support, including document collection, matter tracking and collections and records management. Assist with management of legal matters, including maintaining case files, tracking deadlines, and supporting reporting requirements. Supports the Legal and Compliance technology, processes, and tools, including procedures across the department. Assist with third-party risk management, vendor contracting, and related governance activities. Provides first-level end-user technical support of key legal department systems and introductory end-user training. Creates and collaborates with the Legal team on department presentations, focus meetings, and related requests. Assist with project management and process improvement efforts. Supports broader legal operations responsibilities including regulatory examinations, audits, and compliance initiatives. Plays an active role in advancing Legal Operations initiatives, including process optimization, technology enablement, knowledge management, and department scalability. Other duties as assigned. What You Will Need: High school diploma or equivalent. Bachelor’s degree preferred. Paralegal certificate preferred. 5+ years of related experience. Experience supporting commercial and consumer lending, fintech, payments, sponsor bank, Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS), or other regulated financial services businesses strongly preferred. Experience supporting litigation, bankruptcy and subpoena management preferred. Competencies: Integrity, attention to detail, communication skills, organizational skills The responsibilities listed above are not all inclusive and may be changed at any time. Salary range: $28.80 hourl

Work Location: This position is fully remote and open to candidates residing in the U.S., excluding Alaska; Delaware; Hawaii; Louisiana; Montana; North Dakota; Oklahoma; West Virginia; Wyoming; and U.S. Territories. Daily work is completed from your home office, with occasional travel required for team meetings and company events. #LI-Remote Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $216,108 - $283,642 per year. Chair the Credentialing, Peer Review, and Population Health Management sub-committee, driving individual case reviews and reporting key performance metrics to quarterly Quality Improvement meetings. Oversee practitioner and facility credentialing to guarantee compliance with NCQA standards, CMS requirements, and state regulations - verifying licenses, board certifications, and sanction histories. Partner with Network and Market Management executives to accelerate provider onboarding and strategically resolve network gaps while maintaining strict credentialing integrity. Identify and resolve operational bottlenecks to streamline processes, eliminate delays, and enhance member and provider satisfaction without compromising quality or compliance. Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. Other duties as assigned. Strong knowledge of provider data management, credentialing systems, and primary source verification processes. The US is now our biggest growth opportunity, and this role is central to capturing it. The role We are hiring a Head of Go-to-Market for AI Care Operations in the US. The role sits at the intersection of product marketing, competitive intelligence and commercial enablement. It is one of the leadership roles on the AI Care Operations team, reporting to the General Manager. Here's the opportunity. "AI agents for healthcare" is one of the most crowded categories in the market right now. Voice AI startups, EHR vendors, care management platforms and outsourcers all claim to automate care operations, and to a buyer they can sound alike. Very few of them have certified medical devices, national-scale partnerships, or AI proven on hundreds of thousands of their own members before it was sold to anyone else. We have all three. Your job is to make that difference unmistakable. You will own three things: Make our value impossible to miss.

postings.title: Consultor Emocional Cognitivo-Conductual (Turno Vespertino y fin de semana) .
postings.text: ¿Quiénes somos? Somos el proveedor líder en beneficios de salud mental para colaboradores, brindando servicio a más de 17 millones de personas en todo el mundo y cubriendo 585, 000 vidas en Latinoamérica. Nuestra Cultura y Valores En Lyra transformamos el acceso a atención de salud mental… comprometidos en el día a día con nuestros valores globales; Poner al cliente primero, Seguir la evidencia científica, Ser transparente, Escuchar con atención, Mirar hacia adentro, Enfrentar los retos y Cuidar de ti mismo. Tipo de empleo: Tipo de empleo: 100% Presencial- Oficina en Colonia Nápoles Horario de trabajo: Lunes, Martes y Miercoles de 14:30hrs a 22:30hrs, sábado y domingo de 8:00 hrs a 16;00 hrs. Días de descanso: Jueves y Viernes. Requisitos y Habilidades: -Lic. Psicología con título y cédula profesional con alto sentido de puntualidad y formalidad. -Experiencia clínica de 3 años brindando TCC y/o sistémico (sin contar prácticas o SS). -Disponibilidad para cubrir el periodo de capacitación (pagada) de Martes a viernes de 10:00 a 18:00 hrs y sábados de 12:00 a 20:00 hrs (duración aproximada de 1 mes). -Deseable experiencia en atención al cliente o atención en Call Center. -Deseable experiencia en el manejo de expedientes clínicos digitales. -Deseable experiencia en Call center o brindando terapia por teléfono. Resumen de la posición: El Consultor Emocional es una pieza fundamental para proporcionar atención psicológica de calidad a los clientes de Lyra México y Central America. Este rol requiere de experiencia en psicología clínica (enfoque Cognitivo-Conductual o sistemico) y dominio de la intervención en crisis. El objetivo principal es ofrecer intervenciones basadas en evidencia que ayuden a los clientes a gestionar su bienestar emocional, asegurando una experiencia terapéutica fluida a corto plazo, proporcionando atención profesional . De manera complementaria requiere realización de actividades administrativas para el registro de las atenciones brindadas en la plataforma institucional. Lo que te hace destacar: -Comunicación: Escucha activa, facilidad de palabra, excelente redacción y ortografía. -Proactividad: Capacidad de anticipar, identificar y tomar la iniciativa para resolver situaciones actuando de forma autónoma, trabajo en equipo y eficiente para el uso de todas las herramientas de trabajo a su alcance para lograr soluciones, mejorar procesos y alcanzar objetivos a corto y mediano plazo. Oferta y beneficios: A cambio de tu compromiso y habilidades requeridas del puesto ofrecemos: Salario bruto mensual entre $12,000 y $13,700 Salario mensual bruto dado de alta al 100% ante el IMSS. Prestaciones de Ley. Prestaciones superiores después de periodo de prueba: Aguinaldo de 30 días, Vales de despensa, Vales de restaurante. Bono Anual por desempeño. Plan de salud. Programa de Apoyo a Empleados (orientación psicológica, legal, nutrimental y servicios de información). 4 Días personales semestrales adicionales acorde a las necesidades de la operación. Capacitación anual especializada en psicología clínica acorde a disponibilidad. 3 Días por matrimonio. Ayuda económica anual de útiles escolares para hijos de $1500. Seguro de vida después de un año de trabajo. Canasta navideña $3500. Apoyo económico funerario. Apoyo económico en caso de nacimiento de hijos.

In this role, you may help build AI-assisted capabilities for visit preparation, documentation, summarization, contextual recommendations, and follow-up workflows. You will partner closely with Product, Design, Clinical, Quality, and other engineering teams to take problems from discovery through production. This is an opportunity to work on high-impact, workflow-heavy products where thoughtful technical decisions can improve care-team efficiency, member experience, and Hinge Health’s ability to deliver care at scale. We’re now building a team from the ground up to launch our Gastrointestinal (GI) Care Program. GI conditions affect roughly one in four U.S. adults and drive $135 billion in annual medical spending, yet access to specialized care remains limited. Our planned acquisition of Cylinder Health, a leader in virtual-first digestive healthcare, gives us a strong foundation for entering this market. Together, the teams will combine Cylinder’s clinical expertise and market presence with Hinge Health’s AI-powered care model and technology platform. This is an opportunity for an engineering leader to build a new product from the ground up, shape the future of digital GI care, and define the experience millions of Americans could access through their healthcare plans in 2027. As a Health Economist at Hinge Health, you'll be the analytical engine behind our commercial success—designing and executing rigorous ROI studies that demonstrate how our platform transforms member outcomes while reducing costs for over 20 million lives. Accountable: You balance multiple competing priorities—ad hoc client requests, long-term research projects, and internal cross-functional needs—without dropping the ball. You meet commitments and communicate proactively when timelines shift. Hustler with Rigor: You find creative solutions to data limitations and study design challenges, always delivering defensible, high-quality results that can withstand external scrutiny.
